hints: Focus on what happens to atomic size and electron shielding as you add more shells going down Group 2.
Remember that losing the two outer s-electrons gets easier down the group, so think about how this affects both ionisation energy and reactivity.
Now link this to the hydroxides, recall that $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is almost insoluble while $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ gives a strongly alkaline solution.
walkthrough:
**Check reactivity down the group**

Group 2 metals react by losing their two outer s-electrons to form $\text{M}^{2+}$. Going down, the atoms get larger and there is more shielding.

$$\text{M(s)} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2e^{-}$$

**Check first ionisation energy**

First ionisation energy is the energy to remove the first outer electron. Down the group, the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so attraction is weaker.

$$\text{First IE decreases down Group 2}$$

**Check solubility of hydroxides**

This is a classic Group 2 trend to memorise. Solubility of hydroxides increases down the group. So statement 3 is also true.

$$\text{Mg(OH)}_2 \text{ sparingly soluble} < \text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2 \text{ soluble}$$

**Combine the three statements**

Since statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct descriptions, the option that includes 1, 2 and 3 is the answer.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. Reactivity increases because electrons are lost more easily, first ionisation energy decreases due to increased size and shielding, and Group 2 hydroxides become more soluble down the group.
options.B: Incorrect. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 is also true, so leaving it out is incomplete. Many students forget the solubility trend and think hydroxides become less soluble like the sulfates.
options.C: Incorrect. Statements 2 and 3 are true, but statement 1 is also true. Reactivity does increase down Group 2 because ionisation energies fall and loss of electrons becomes easier.
options.D: Incorrect. Statement 1 alone is true but incomplete. Statements 2 and 3 are also correct trends, so an option with only statement 1 misses two valid trends.
